Fixed. The root cause: `@StandardException`'s generated constructors delegate via `this(null, null)`. When another lombok-generated constructor with exactly two reference parameters exists (e.g. `@AllArgsConstructor` on a class with two object fields), `null` matches both overloads and javac reports ambiguity. The fix casts the `null` arguments so the delegation always unambiguously resolves to the `(String, Throwable)` constructor:

- `src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleStandardException.java` — no-arg constructor now delegates with `this((java.lang.String) null, (java.lang.Throwable) null)`; msg-only constructor delegates the cause as `(java.lang.Throwable) null`.
- `src/core/lombok/eclipse/handlers/HandleStandardException.java` — same fix for the ecj handler via a `createCastToNull` helper producing `CastExpression(QualifiedTypeReference, NullLiteral)`.

Validation:
- `ant compile` — success
- `ant test.javacCurrent` — all pass, including `StandardExceptions`/`StandardExceptionWithConstructor` transform tests
- `ant test.eclipse-oxygen` — all ecj transform tests pass
- Manual end-to-end: the issue's reproduce case (`@StandardException` + `@AllArgsConstructor` with two object fields) now compiles, and delombok shows the expected cast delegation
